about.lead: A site that gathers the cell types of the human body and links them into a network based on the Cell Ontology.
about.method1: English names, definitions and relationships (is_a, develops_from) are fetched from the Cell Ontology through the EBI OLS API by a script, which also checks that IDs are valid, not obsolete, and that names match CL.
about.method2: Thai content (morphology, function, exam points, diseases) and links that CL does not have (such as how cells work together) are written by hand and stored as JSON files. Fields that are uncertain are left empty rather than guessed.
about.method3: Every entry has a verified / not-yet-verified status. Thai content counts as verified only after it has been checked against textbooks such as Junqueira's Basic Histology and Campbell Biology.
about.method4: Every build produces a report comparing the hand-curated links with the Cell Ontology so that differences can be reviewed and decided on.
about.methodTitle: How the data is collected and checked
about.olsCredit: The service used to fetch data from the Cell Ontology.
about.project1: Nexus · Cell Web is made for students preparing for medical school entrance exams and anyone curious about cell biology. It puts the cell types of the human body into one web that you can explore by organ system, as a whole-body overview, or by tissue, with a quiz mode and a cell comparison tool.
about.project2: Every cell is identified by its Cell Ontology ID (CL ID). The Thai content is written by the project author. The site is bilingual (Thai and English) and works offline.
